Near k2=0 and k2=k1, the bond-filtered inverse trace is 4/[A(t²+6delta)] locally, giving each of two lines coefficient T_*sqrt(2/3)/A. The k1=0 line is killed by the bond filter. A polar estimate sqrt(delta)*int_{r<eta}F<=C(eta+sqrt(delta)) rules out additional intersection mass. Every bounded continuous torus test function therefore has the asserted weak limit. The sharp coefficient and the equal concentration on precisely two pressure-softened reciprocal lines quantify a meaningful experimentally interpretable bond-compliance divergence and reveal its geometric origin. This is a nonuniform soft-manifold spectral result and not a mere reformulation of the known instability threshold or a routine fixed-parameter integral.
